item.title: How the war in Iran turned the Gulf into a climate catastrophe – video explainer
item.description: The war between the US, Israel and Iran has turned the strait of Hormuz, one of the world’s busiest oil shipping routes, into a battlefield, but also the centre of a deepening environmental disaster. Tankers struck by missiles or sea mines are leaking oil into the Gulf, leaving vast slicks visible from space, staining coastlines and threatening lasting damage to marine ecosystems. Many of these areas remain inaccessible because of the naval blockade, making it virtually impossible to document the devastation on the ground. item.description: Iraq has reached ​a compromise with the powerful Iran-backed militia Kataib Hezbollah, three senior security officials said, after Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi readied security forces to move against the group. item.title: Outcry as fossil fuels scrubbed from draft UN climate deal
item.description: UN climate talks co-host Australia unveiled a new draft agreement Thursday that drops any mention of fossil fuels, the leading driver of global warming, sparking anger from campaign groups. The nearly 200 nations involved in the COP31 global climate talks in Turkey have until Friday to strike a final agreement, though the marathon negotiations often run into overtime. The summit is unfolding against a record-breaking El Nino, disasters fuelled by climate change from Europe to Nepal and a global energy shock triggered by the Iran war. Fuente: France 24 - English.
